; DNS records for example.com — add them at your DNS provider.
; Format: name  type  value

; WHAT TO ADD — one block below = one record in your provider's form
;
;   Type: A
;   Name: relay   — most panels want just relay — some want the full relay.example.com
;   Value: 203.0.113.10
;   TTL: Auto (or 3600)
;
;   Type: A
;   Name: cloud   — most panels want just cloud — some want the full cloud.example.com
;   Value: 203.0.113.10
;   TTL: Auto (or 3600)
;
;   Type: A
;   Name: vault   — most panels want just vault — some want the full vault.example.com
;   Value: 203.0.113.10
;   TTL: Auto (or 3600)
;
; Cloudflare: set Proxy status to "DNS only" (grey cloud) for EVERY record here. The orange cloud breaks mail and the VPN.
;
; IMPORT INSTEAD OF TYPING
; Cloudflare: DNS → Records → "Import and Export" → "Import DNS records" → upload example.com-dns-zone.txt.
; Then check every imported record is "DNS only" (grey cloud).
; The same example.com-dns-zone.txt works at Route53, Google, Namecheap, GoDaddy, Gandi, Hetzner, deSEC, DNSimple, Porkbun.
; Panels that ask for a spreadsheet instead: use example.com-dns-records.csv.


; Forward record for the PTR hostname (reverse DNS must resolve back to the same IP).
relay.example.com.    IN A    203.0.113.10

; Service hostnames — the same public IP of the VPS (proxied by Caddy).
cloud.example.com.    IN A    203.0.113.10
vault.example.com.    IN A    203.0.113.10

; PTR (reverse DNS) is configured NOT here but in the VPS provider's panel:
; 203.0.113.10 -> relay.example.com — critical for deliverability.
